Subject: Renewal options + pilot proposal (multi-year + staged uplift)

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the productive sync yesterday. Per our conversation, I pulled together three paths that balance AtlasCloud's runway needs with predictable unit economics: a short summary below and a detailed options spreadsheet attached (Redwood_Renewal_Options_Table_v2.xlsx).

High-level options
- Option A (Conservative): 1-year renewal, co-term to calendar year, 25% burst buffer, standard monthly billing.
- Option B (Staged Uplift): 3-year term, year-over-year ramp (20% / 30% / 40%), escrowed first-year usage credits to offset onboarding peak, optional early-burst tranche unlocked on pilot success.
- Option C (Pilot-first): 12-month contract + 90-day canary pilot on reserved capacity; if pilot meets SLAs, convert to 3-year staged uplift with a one-time onboarding credit.

My recommendation for AtlasCloud based on your growth forecast is Option B with a 60-day canary window before year 1 ramp completes. This gives you predictable unit cost while preserving a built-in early-burst path to handle marketing-driven spikes.

Next steps I propose:
1) Share the attached amendment draft (Draft_Amendment_Escrow_Uplift_v1.docx) with your procurement for feedback.
2) Confirm whether you want co-terming to calendar year or to your fiscal year.
3) If you prefer the pilot-first route, we can schedule a capacity carve-out (estimated 2 extra A100-equivalent nodes) for the 90-day window.

I'll loop in Rishi and Karthik to help with pricing nuance and finance approval notes.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz

Sarah —

Great questions. Quick replies inline and next steps below.

- Escrow/redemption: The proposed escrow is an accounting hold (funds applied to a ledger credit line) that automatically reduces invoiceable tokens until exhausted. We'll surface a statement-of-credits on each invoice and provide a running balance via the Console. Karthik has a short note in the attached amendment (see section 2.1 redemption mechanics).

- Frontloading: Yes — we can scaffold the pilot with a frontloaded 30-day credit tranche (up to 40% of the pilot capacity) to cover onboarding bursts. The remainder of the escrow stays locked for later months.

- Auto-renew: We can flip default to opt-in; proposed language: "Contracts will not auto-renew unless both parties opt-in in writing 45 days prior to term end." We track that as an optional clause in the amendment.

Attached: small revision to the amendment with the redemption flow clarified.

If you're comfortable, can you (a) confirm co-term preference (calendar vs. fiscal) and (b) indicate whether procurement wants any additional invoice-level detail (PO number placement, vendor remittance instructions)? If procurement prefers, I can move redlines into DocuSign-friendly track changes.

Thanks — looping in Rishi to align on the staged uplift and Marissa for post-sales continuity.

Vanessa

Thanks Vanessa / Sarah — I like the staged uplift with escrowed credits. A few pragmatic tweaks from a commercial governance perspective:

1) Performance-triggered uplift: add a small performance tranche (5% of year-2 capacity) that unlocks when mean latency < 250ms and error-rate < 1% during the 90-day pilot. This aligns incentives and protects our capacity.
2) Escrow accounting: recommend we put a ledger note in Year 1 that converts escrow to credits on a monthly amortization schedule (helps procurement forecast).
3) Billing cadence: allow AtlasCloud to pick either monthly invoices or quarterly invoicing at slightly different pricing tiers — we can show both in table.

Marissa — can you prep a short onboarding checklist and a 90-day success criteria doc for the pilot (console telemetry, SLOs, launch checklist)? We'll attach that to the amendment as Exhibit A.

Sarah — once procurement confirms co-term preference, we can bake that into the DocuSign packet and route to legal. If procurement wants, finance can produce a sample invoice that shows the escrow redemption line.

Cheers,
